Difference-in-Differences in Distribution Functions

Source: R/cdf_did.R
cdf_did.Rd

Computes the Quantile Treatment Effect on the Treated (QTT) and the Average Treatment Effect on the Treated (ATT) under parallel trends in the distribution functions of untreated potential outcomes, with staggered treatment adoption, for panel data or repeated cross sections.

Identification. For each group \(g\) and period \(t\), $$F_{Y_t(0)|G=g}(y) - F_{Y_{t-1}(0)|G=g}(y) = F_{Y_t(0)|C}(y) - F_{Y_{t-1}(0)|C}(y) \quad \text{for all } y,$$ with \(C\) the comparison group: parallel trends for the distribution function rather than the mean (DiD) or the quantile function (QDiD). Roth and Sant'Anna (2023) show this is the condition under which parallel trends holds for every transformation of the outcome. It point-identifies the counterfactual distribution, so the QTT, for discrete outcomes too, and the implied ATT is the usual DiD ATT. Covariates make the assumption conditional on \(X\).

See cdf_did_gt for how the counterfactual distribution is estimated (including the rearrangement into a valid distribution function and the three covariate methods).

Usage

cdf_did(
  yname,
  gname,
  tname,
  idname = NULL,
  data,
  panel = TRUE,
  xformula = ~1,
  est_method = c("aipw", "ipw", "reg"),
  weightsname = NULL,
  clustervars = NULL,
  control_group = "notyettreated",
  anticipation = 0,
  alp = 0.05,
  cband = TRUE,
  biters = 100,
  cl = 1,
  gt_type = c("att", "qtt"),
  probs = NULL
)

Arguments

yname

Name of the outcome variable in data.

gname

Name of the treatment group variable (first treatment period; 0 for never-treated units).

tname

Name of the time period variable.

idname

Name of the unit id variable. Required when panel = TRUE.

data

A data frame.

panel

Logical. TRUE (default) for panel data; FALSE for repeated cross sections (see the section on repeated cross sections).

xformula

One-sided formula of covariates. Default ~1. With panel data, each unit's covariates are taken from the base period of each group-time cell (never from a post-treatment period); with repeated cross sections, each observation's own values are used.

est_method

With covariates: "aipw" (default; doubly robust), "ipw" or "reg" (outcome regression, as in did).

weightsname

Name of the column in data containing sampling weights. Default NULL uses equal weights.

clustervars

Name of a column in data to cluster standard errors on, in addition to idname (as in did::att_gt()). With the empirical bootstrap, whole clusters are resampled.

control_group

"notyettreated" (default) or "nevertreated".

anticipation

Number of time periods before treatment during which units may anticipate it. Default 0.

alp

Significance level. Default 0.05.

cband

Logical; uniform confidence bands. Default TRUE.

biters

Number of bootstrap iterations. Default 100.

cl

Number of cores for the bootstrap. Default 1.

gt_type

"att" (default) for the ATT and event study, or "qtt" for the QTT curve.

probs

For gt_type = "qtt", the quantiles at which to report the QTT. Default seq(0.05, 0.95, 0.05).

Value

For gt_type = "att", a pte_emp_boot object; for gt_type = "qtt", a pte_qtt object. Both include outcome_discreteness.

Discrete outcomes

The counterfactual distribution is identified for discrete outcomes as well, unlike for rank- or quantile-based estimators such as cic. Quantile effects still jump at mass points and their bootstrap inference can be unreliable, so gt_type = "qtt" warns (once per call) when the outcome looks discrete; see cic.

Repeated cross sections

cic(), qdid(), mdid(), cdf_did() and lou_qtt(lagged_outcome_cov = FALSE) also work with repeated cross sections (panel = FALSE; idname not needed). Without covariates they use only each period's outcome distributions, so on panel data the estimates are the same either way; the standard errors differ, because the bootstrap then resamples observations rather than units. Some things need the same units in several periods and so require panel data: ddid() (each comparison unit's change over time), panel_qtt() (the copula between periods), the lagged outcome in lou_qtt(), and gt_type = "qott" (the distribution of individual treatment effects).

References

Roth, Jonathan, and Pedro H. C. Sant'Anna. “When Is Parallel Trends Sensitive to Functional Form?” Econometrica 91(2), pp. 737-747, 2023.

Sant'Anna, Pedro H. C., and Jun Zhao. “Doubly Robust Difference-in-Differences Estimators.” Journal of Econometrics 219(1), pp. 101-122, 2020.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(mpdta, package = "did")
res <- cdf_did(yname = "lemp", gname = "first.treat", tname = "year",
               idname = "countyreal", data = mpdta, gt_type = "qtt",
               probs = seq(0.1, 0.9, 0.1), biters = 20)
summary(res)
